label: SoundnessBench_general_c5_v3
original_text: We will intentionally introduce severe methodological flaws (e.g., mismatched datasets and metrics) into high-soundness proposals to test if models can detect these obvious errors.
modified_text: We will intentionally introduce severe methodological flaws by replacing the name of a standard dataset (e.g., ImageNet) with one from a completely unrelated domain (e.g., the General Social Survey) to test if models can detect these obvious errors.
explanation: This modification makes the "severe flaw" syntactically trivial to detect. The task is reduced from methodological reasoning to a simple named-entity-to-domain matching exercise. An LLM does not need to understand *why* using a sociology dataset for an image recognition task is methodologically unsound; it only needs to recognize from its training data that "ImageNet" belongs to computer vision and "General Social Survey" does not. This test would be an invalid proxy because it evaluates a form of knowledge retrieval or topic modeling, not the nuanced reasoning required to identify plausible-but-incorrect methodological choices within the correct domain (e.g., using a biased dataset for a fairness claim).
reasoning: The error arises because the proposed operationalization of "severe methodological flaw" (syntactic name mismatch) diverges from the intended meaning of "methodological reasoning," making the test an invalid proxy.
